name: Tola
overview: Tola is a male judge of Israel from the tribe of Issachar. He is noted in Scripture as a descendant of Issachar who arose to save Israel. His role as a judge signifies a God-ordained leadership position during a critical period in Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: The name Tola means '(deep) red, purple' in Hebrew. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but is recorded in Judges 10:1.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Tola was the son of Puah. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are mentioned in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Tola's significance lies in his role as a judge who delivered Israel, highlighting God's providential care through chosen leaders. As a descendant of Issachar, he represents the tribe's contribution to Israel's governance and deliverance during a time of need. His leadership is briefly noted but underscores the ongoing cycle of judges raised by God to preserve His covenant people.
